lessons.title: Adab in our live lessons
objectives: Say why we listen to each other
Practise good adab in a live lesson
Link adab to the value of Excellence (ihsan)

keywords.def: good manners and behaviour
treating others with care
to pay attention with your ears and eyes
doing your best because Allah sees you

starter: Bismillah. Show me a kind hand.
Name one thing you can do to be kind.

teach.heading: The Tarbiyyah Compass and adab
bullets: Our school values are called the Tarbiyyah Compass
teach.note: Introduce the Tarbiyyah Compass simply: Resilience, Eeman, Contentment, Integrity, Progress, Excellence. Today's focus is Excellence and adab. Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Pupils may ask anonymous questions via the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day.

teach.heading: Adab in a live lesson
bullets: Put up your hand to speak
teach.note: Model each action. Misconception: adab is only for school; it is for everywhere.

teach.heading: Kind chat and talking
bullets: Mute until it is your turn
teach.note: Practise unmuting politely. Ask 'how does it feel when everyone talks at once?'

teach.heading: Doing our best
bullets: Try your best even when it is hard
Allah loves when we do our best
teach.note: Cite plainly: ihsan means to do things in the best way. Keep language simple.

practice: Why do we put up a hand?
independent: Show good adab for starting a lesson: salaam, look, listen.
Role-play asking the teacher a question.
exit: Make a poster with three adab rules.
Tell a grown-up one rule you will keep.
homework: Name one rule for live lessons.
lessons.send: Show your family your adab poster and teach them one rule.

lessons.title: Friends and solving problems kindly
objectives: Say what makes a good friend
Use words to solve a problem

keywords.def: someone who is kind and plays with you
something that is hard or not working
to find a way to fix a problem
to stop being cross with someone

starter: Say one kind sentence to a friend.
What do you do when you are cross?

teach.heading: Good friends
teach.note: Ask who plays with whom. Stress including everyone. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said the best of you are those best in character (Sahih al-Bukhari). Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Pupils may ask anonymous questions via the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day.

teach.heading: Solving problems
bullets: Ask a grown-up if you need help
teach.note: Role-play an argument over a toy, using two name cards for the two sides. Model calm voice. Misconception: hitting or shouting solves problems.

teach.heading: Sorry and forgiveness
bullets: Sorry means I will try to do better
teach.note: Teach the phrase 'It's okay, I forgive you'. Keep it sincere; no forced apologies.

teach.heading: Kindness plan
teach.note: Children choose from a list: share, help, smile, say thank you.

practice: What can you say instead of shouting?
independent: Practise using words to solve a pretend problem.
Draw two speech bubbles showing what two friends could say to solve a problem.
exit: Draw a problem (such as a broken toy) and how to solve it kindly, using objects and speech bubbles.
Write or say one kind sentence.
homework: Give one way to solve a problem.
lessons.send: Do one kind act and tell the class about it.

lessons.title: My body belongs to me
objectives: Know that our bodies belong to us
Know to tell a trusted adult if something feels wrong

keywords.def: just for you, not for others to see or touch
all of you, from head to toe
a grown-up you can ask for help
not safe, giving you a worried feeling

teach.heading: My body is mine
teach.note: Use calm and simple language. Use proper words where needed. Parents have been told in advance via the Parent Portal. Do not ask children to describe any personal experiences. Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Pupils may ask anonymous questions via the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day.

teach.heading: Private parts are private
bullets: The parts covered by underwear are private
No one should look at or touch them unless to keep us clean or healthy
Doctors or parents can help in safe ways
teach.note: Use only the minimum language needed. Give the rule: private means private. Link to modesty (haya) in Islam.

teach.heading: Safe and unsafe
teach.note: Ask them to show thumbs up or down for example situations (a hug from a parent versus a stranger asking to see a toy).

teach.heading: Tell a trusted adult
bullets: Go away and tell a grown-up
teach.note: Stress it is never the child's fault. Teach 'Say no, go, tell'. Secrets that make you feel unsafe must be told.

practice: Who can you tell if you feel unsafe?
independent: Practise saying 'no, go, tell' with a grown-up at home.
exit: Draw your five trusted people on your hand.
Tell a grown-up your 'no, go, tell' plan.
homework: Is it your fault if someone makes you feel unsafe?
What do you do if you feel unsafe?
lessons.send: Share your safe hand with a family member and talk about who you would tell.

lessons.title: Online safety: ask first, be kind
objectives: Know to ask before clicking or downloading
Know to tell a grown-up about worries

keywords.def: connected to the internet
check with a grown-up before you click
to press with a mouse or tap with a finger
hurtful or not caring

starter: Bismillah. What do we do if something worries us on a screen?

teach.heading: The online world
bullets: Many websites and games are safe
teach.note: Ask what children do online. Stay positive and calm. Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Pupils may ask anonymous questions via the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day.

teach.heading: Ask first
bullets: Ask before you tell your name
teach.note: Practise a pop-up scenario. 'Win a prize' pop-ups are tricks. Misconception: if it is on a screen it must be safe.

teach.heading: Be kind online
bullets: Use kind words in games and chat
Tell a grown-up if someone is unkind
teach.note: Link to adab and kind friends. Write a kind message together.

teach.heading: Tell a grown-up
bullets: You will not be in trouble
teach.note: Repeat the safety message. Show a 'stop and tell' sign.

practice: What do we do before we click?
What do we do if someone is unkind online?
independent: Sort pictures into 'ask first' and 'safe to do'.
exit: Make a poster: 'Ask first, be kind, tell'.
Say your poster rules to a grown-up.
homework: What should you do before downloading?
Who can you tell if you feel worried?
lessons.send: Teach your family your online safety rules.

lessons.title: Keeping clean: hands and teeth
lessons.bigQuestion: Germs are too small to see. How do we know they are on our hands?
objectives: To understand why keeping our hands and teeth clean keeps us healthy
successCriteria: All: show the steps of handwashing on camera
Most: say two times we must wash our hands
Some: explain how germs spread and how the miswak and toothbrush help
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: cleanliness (taharah) as part of faith

keywords.def: tiny living things that can make us ill
keeping ourselves clean
a twig used to clean the teeth (مِسْوَاك)
well and strong

hook.text: Germs are too small to see. How do we know they are on our hands?
hook.a: We cannot see them, but we can wash them away with soap and water.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ taught that cleanliness is half of faith (Muslim). He loved the miswak and said that if it were not hard on his people, he would have told them to use it before every prayer (al-Bukhari and Muslim).

starter.q: Show me: what do we say before we eat?
Show me: one way to be kind in our lesson.
starter.a: For example: listen, wait our turn, kind words.

starter.q: Is a fruit a healthy snack? Thumbs up or down.

teach.heading: What are germs?
bullets: They live on hands and in mouths
teach.note: Use the glitter idea: sprinkle a little glitter (or flour) on your hand, shake a toy, show it spread.

teach.heading: Wash your hands
teach.note: Do it slowly on camera at a sink or with a bowl. Count to 20 while rubbing.

teach.heading: Clean teeth
teach.note: Show a miswak and a toothbrush.

check.q: When must we wash our hands?
options: After playing a game on the sofa
check.why: Before eating (and after the toilet) stops germs getting into our mouths.

practice.q: Show me the handwashing steps with your hands (no water).
practice.a: Wet, soap, rub backs, fingers and thumbs, rinse, dry.
practice.model: Teacher mimes each step slowly and counts to 20 while rubbing.

practice.q: Say two times we wash our hands.
practice.a: Before eating and after the toilet (also after playing outside).

independent.q: Core: Go to a sink with a grown-up and wash your hands properly, counting to 20. Come back and give a thumbs up.
independent.model: Teacher shows where the soap goes on the backs of the hands.

independent.q: Extend: Draw a toothbrush and a miswak and colour them in (objects only).
independent.a: A labelled drawing of a toothbrush and a miswak.

exit.q: Germs are... A) tiny and can make us ill B) big and friendly C) only on toys
exit.a: A) tiny and can make us ill
options: Tiny and can make us ill

exit.q: Big question: how do we get germs off our hands?
exit.a: Wash with soap and water for 20 seconds.

lessons.homework: Brush your teeth twice a day this week and tick a chart (pupil PDF) with your grown-up.
lessons.send: SEND: picture cards for each handwashing step. EAL: wash, soap, germs with actions. Stretch: say why we wash for 20 seconds.

Soap, water, towel at home (a grown-up helps)
Toothbrush and a miswak to show
A pinch of glitter or flour for the germs demonstration

lessons.title: Staying healthy: food, water, sleep and moving
lessons.bigQuestion: If your body was a car, what would its fuel be?
objectives: To understand that food, water, sleep and moving our bodies help us stay healthy
successCriteria: All: name one healthy food and one treat
Most: say why we need water and sleep
Some: set one small healthy goal for the week
lessons.smsc: Moral: looking after the body as an amanah

keywords.def: good for our body
a food we have only sometimes
rest our body needs every night
something we try to do

hook.text: If your body was a car, what would its fuel be?
hook.a: Healthy food and water; and sleep is like parking it to rest.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Eat and drink, but do not waste by excess' (al-A'raf 7:31). Our bodies are a trust (amanah) from Allah, so we look after them.

starter.q: Show me: how long do we rub our hands with soap?
Show me: what do we use to clean our teeth?
Thumbs up or down: germs can make us ill.

teach.heading: Food
bullets: Say Bismillah and eat with the right hand
teach.note: Sort the foods.

teach.heading: Water and sleep
bullets: Water helps us think and play
Bedtime after Isha, early to rise
teach.note: Children of this age need about 10 to 12 hours of sleep.

teach.heading: Moving
teach.note: Do a 30-second stretch together (no music).

check.why: Sweets are fine sometimes; fruit and vegetables are for every day.

practice.q: Show me: draw one healthy food on your whiteboard.
practice.a: For example: an apple, a carrot, a banana.
practice.model: Teacher draws a banana and says 'every day food'.

practice.q: Thumbs up or down: we need sleep to grow.

independent.q: Core: Draw your healthy plate: three foods for every day (pupil PDF).
independent.a: A plate with three healthy foods.
independent.model: Teacher draws the first food on the plate.

independent.q: Extend: Choose one goal: drink water with every meal, or a fruit every day. Tell the class.

exit.q: Our body needs... A) only sweets B) food, water, sleep and moving C) only sleep
exit.a: B) food, water, sleep and moving

exit.q: Big question: what is our body's fuel?

lessons.homework: Try your goal every day this week and show your grown-up.
lessons.send: SEND: real or picture food cards to sort. EAL: food words with pictures. Stretch: say why water helps us.
